sql:
SELECT COUNT(1) AS n
FROM   TPCDS_DB.item i
WHERE  i.i_current_price > (SELECT AVG(i2.i_current_price) FROM TPCDS_DB.item i2 WHERE i2.i_category = i.i_category)

attempts.change_summary: Replaced correlated subquery with single scan using window function to compute per-category averages, eliminating second table scan and broadcast join.

diagnosis.bottleneck: The correlated subquery forces two full scans of the item table (nodes 1 and 3) and a broadcast hash join (node 10) that processes every outer row against the per-category averages, resulting in doubled I/O and a join that could be avoided with a single-pass aggregation.

hypotheses.claim: A correlated subquery is re-evaluated per outer row (or decorrelated into a costly join). (matched: (select avg(i2.i_current_price) from tpcds_db.item i2 where i2.i_category = i.i_category))
Scanning the entire item table twice (nodes 1 and 3) doubles the I/O from S3; a single scan with a window function or a precomputed aggregate would halve the data read.

The broadcast hash join compares each outer row's price to the category average; if the outer table is large, the per-row comparison and hash lookup add CPU overhead that could be eliminated by pushing the filter into a single aggregated scan.

The partial aggregate (node 5) and subsequent shuffle (node 6) to compute category averages may cause unnecessary data movement; a map-side aggregation or a partition-by-category scan could avoid the shuffle.
